title: Sections vanishing on a closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a proper $k$-scheme, $\mathcal L$ an ample invertible sheaf on $Y$, and $Z\subset Y$ a closed subscheme. For all sufficiently large $n$, the kernel $V_n$ of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal L^{\otimes n}|_Z)$ generates $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ on $Y\setminus Z$, and the associated morphism $Y\setminus Z\to\mathbf P(V_n)$ is an immersion.
Here properness, ampleness, invertibility, and schemes are understood in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-sc-ample], [def-sc-invertible-module], with generation by sections as in [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], the associated morphism to $\mathbf P(V_n)$ (over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with coordinates indexed by a basis of $V_n$) as in [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], and immersions as in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text: Properness over the field gives a locally Noetherian source. Its closed-subscheme ideal is quasi-coherent and finitely presented. Apply Serre generation to obtain a bound a for all ideal twists. The proved library theorem exists_generatingSections_tensorObj_tensorPow applies directly to the relative ample predicate; no conversion to absolute ampleness is needed.

Define the complement U to be the complement of the support of the closed-immersion kernel ideal. The support formula for this ideal identifies its complement pointwise with the complement of the closed immersion image.

In degree n define V as the actual submodule killed by pullback to Z. The ideal-tensor sections theorem identifies it with the image of ideal multiplication; compare adjunctions by uniqueness to obtain the formula for the standard pullback unit. On U the ideal inclusion is an isomorphism. The ideal-twist evaluation is thus epi after restriction and after pullback.

Proper coherent cohomology makes the section space finite dimensional. Choose a finite basis of the submodule V. Constant linear combinations give an explicit factorization of the ideal evaluation through the free sheaf on this basis. Its pullback is epi by cancellation. Evaluate the basis sections at the top open to prove their span and linear independence, and use the pullback-free comparison to construct the restricted sections and their value formula.

Choose a positive very ample power r from the relative ample hypothesis and set the eventual bound to a+r. For n at least this bound, both n and n-r exceed a. Apply the product-system immersion criterion to the degree n-r ideal-twist generators, the fixed degree r very ample embedding, and the constructed degree n basis system. Its span condition is exactly basis spanning of V; its value condition is the proved pullback-free formula. This supplies the immersion and completes all existential clauses.
